# Trail Preparation

Before setting out on a long hike, check the weather forecast and trail
conditions, and let someone know your planned route and expected return
time. Pack enough water, high energy snacks, a map or GPS device, and a
first aid kit. Break in your hiking boots well before a big trip to
avoid blisters, and pack layers so you can adjust to changing
temperatures as you gain elevation.

# Mountain Safety

Weather in the mountains can change quickly, so watch the sky for
building storm clouds and be ready to turn back if conditions worsen.
Stay on marked trails to avoid getting lost, and carry a whistle and a
headlamp in case you are caught out after dark. If you encounter
wildlife, keep your distance and never approach or feed the animals you
meet along the trail.
